current_row.boundary_rationale: a setumah closes oshb:Jer.44.23 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), marking the preceding unit's own close immediately before this span's own opening. The ironic reply to their own vow-language follows, telling them to keep the vows they swore to the queen of the sky, כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָֽה צְבָאוֹת֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֵאמֹ֗ר אַתֶּ֨ם וּנְשֵׁיכֶ֜ם וַתְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה בְּפִיכֶם֮ וּבִידֵיכֶ֣ם מִלֵּאתֶ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ עָשֹׂ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה אֶת נְדָרֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָדַ֨רְנוּ֙ לְקַטֵּר֙ לִמְלֶ֣כֶת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְהַסֵּ֥ךְ לָ֖הּ נְסָכִ֑ים הָקֵ֤ים תָּקִ֨ימְנָה֙ אֶת נִדְרֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָשֹׂ֥ה תַעֲשֶׂ֖ינָה אֶת נִדְרֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.44.25, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, 'You and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and with your hands have fulfilled it, saying, "We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to her." "'Establish then your vows, and perform your vows.'” (web:Jer.44.25) -- WEB's own layout marks a paragraph fold inside this verse (tier-4 metadata, not evidence for or against a boundary); a petuchah closes oshb:Jer.44.25 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum). The oath proper reopens on lakhen shim'u devar YHWH, echoing this span's own opening imperative rather than a fresh narrative tag reintroducing the speaker, לָכֵן֙ שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה כָּל יְהוּדָ֕ה הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הִנְנִ֨י נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי בִּשְׁמִ֤י הַגָּדוֹל֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם יִהְיֶה֩ ע֨וֹד שְׁמִ֜י נִקְרָ֣א בְּפִ֣י כָּל אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֹמֵ֛ר חַי אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה בְּכָל אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.44.26, byte), matching “Therefore hear Yahweh's word, all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: 'Behold, I have sworn by my great name,' says Yahweh, 'that my name will no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, "” (web:Jer.44.26) the formula Judah's own men will no longer be able to swear is quoted next, “As the Lord Yahweh lives."” (web:Jer.44.26) the divine title's qamats-pointed form (one of 11 divine-title adonai sites, sweep: 11 of 13 verses, point-aware against the two courtly hiriq sites addressed to Zedekiah elsewhere in the book); four paseq segs stand across this span -- one at oshb:Jer.44.25, two here at oshb:Jer.44.26, and one at oshb:Jer.44.30 (single-witness, seg layer, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). The negative and positive halves of the sentence follow without a break, הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁקֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָעָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א לְטוֹבָ֑ה וְתַמּוּ֩ כָל אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֶ֥רֶב וּבָרָעָ֖ב עַד כְּלוֹתָֽם (oshb:Jer.44.27, byte), matching “Behold, I watch over them for evil, and not for good; and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until they are all gone.” (web:Jer.44.27) and וּפְלִיטֵ֨י חֶ֜רֶב יְשֻׁב֨וּן מִן אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה הַבָּאִ֤ים לְאֶֽרֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם דְּבַר מִ֥י יָק֖וּם מִמֶּ֥נִּי וּמֵהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.44.28, byte), matching “Those who escape the sword will return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah few in number. All the remnant of Judah, who have gone into the land of Egypt to live there, will know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.” (web:Jer.44.28) The sign formula opens next, וְזֹאת לָכֶ֤ם הָאוֹת֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי פֹקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּ כִּי֩ ק֨וֹם יָק֧וּמוּ דְבָרַ֛י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְרָעָֽה (oshb:Jer.44.29, byte), matching “"'This will be the sign to you,' says Yahweh, 'that I will punish you in this place, that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for evil.'” (web:Jer.44.29) a setumah closes oshb:Jer.44.29 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), disclosed as texture rather than as this span's own end. current_row.boundary_rationale: a setumah closes oshb:Jer.44.30 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), marking the preceding chapter's own close immediately before this span's own opening. A header opens this closing oracle of the frame, dated inside its own verse to Jehoiakim's fourth year rather than to the post-Gedaliah setting just narrated, הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל בָּר֖וּךְ בֶּֽן נֵֽרִיָּ֑ה בְּכָתְבוֹ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה עַל סֵ֨פֶר֙ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֧ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֛הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.45.1, byte), matching “The message that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,” (web:Jer.45.1) its own shape reads asher DIBBER ("which he spoke"), not asher HAYAH ("which came") -- a construction of its own, held apart from the 11-verse hadavar-asher-hayah list named above at this frame's own opening sermon (sweep: 11 verses); a setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.1 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum) too, disclosed as texture. The address to Baruch by name follows at once, כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עָלֶ֖יךָ בָּרֽוּךְ (oshb:Jer.45.2, byte), matching “"Yahweh, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:” (web:Jer.45.2) and his own complaint is quoted back to him, אָמַ֨רְתָּ֙ אֽוֹי נָ֣א לִ֔י כִּֽי יָסַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה יָג֖וֹן עַל מַכְאֹבִ֑י יָגַ֨עְתִּי֙ בְּאַנְחָתִ֔י וּמְנוּחָ֖ה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי (oshb:Jer.45.3, byte), matching “'You said, "Woe is me now! For Yahweh has added sorrow to my pain! I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest."'” (web:Jer.45.3) the cry oy na li ("woe is me now") here is the distinct aleph-lexeme oy (sweep: 8 verses book-wide), not the vav-initial hoy of this book's woe-oracle and funeral-cry system -- a bare woe-token sweep would blend the two; a setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.3 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), disclosed as texture rather than adopted as a driver for a cut at this exact point. The response proper opens on koh tomar eilav ("thus you shall tell him"), a relay imperative inside the same commission to Jeremiah rather than a fresh command of its own -- the same shape as ve'amarta aleihem at oshb:Jer.43.10 earlier in this frame, kept inside its own governing address on the same reasoning -- כֹּ֣ה תֹּאמַ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֤ה אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֨יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י הֹרֵ֔ס וְאֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר נָטַ֖עְתִּי אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֑שׁ וְאֶת כָּל הָאָ֖רֶץ הִֽיא (oshb:Jer.45.4, byte), matching “"You shall tell him, Yahweh says: 'Behold, that which I have built, I will break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up; and this in the whole land.” (web:Jer.45.4) a paseq falls in this verse (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The oracle closes on Baruch's own life granted him amid the judgment named in the same verse, וְאַתָּ֛ה תְּבַקֶּשׁ לְךָ֥ גְדֹל֖וֹת אַל תְּבַקֵּ֑שׁ כִּ֡י הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא רָעָ֤ה עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְנָתַתִּ֨י לְךָ֤ אֶֽת נַפְשְׁךָ֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל עַ֥ל כָּל הַמְּקֹמ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּֽלֶךְ שָֽׁם (oshb:Jer.45.5, byte), matching “Do you seek great things for yourself? Don't seek them; for, behold, I will bring evil on all flesh,' says Yahweh, 'but I will let you escape with your life wherever you go.'"” (web:Jer.45.5) closing not on that formula, which stands mid-verse, but on the life-grant clause that follows it in the same verse, paired here with the fresh onset that follows at oshb:Jer.46.1. a setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.5 (single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), closing this span's own end verse, together with the chapter and this frame. current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.5 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own opening on the nations-rubric that stands over the whole collection, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם (oshb:Jer.46.1, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) — one of only four verses in the book carrying this exact asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu shape (sweep: 4 verses), naming Jeremiah before naming any single nation. Egypt's own header follows at once with its date folded inside the same verse, לְמִצְרַ֗יִם עַל חֵ֨יל פַּרְעֹ֤ה נְכוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה עַל נְהַר פְּרָ֖ת בְּכַרְכְּמִ֑שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte), matching “Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah.” (web:Jer.46.2) — Pharaoh Necoh, the Euphrates, Carchemish, and Nebuchadnezzar (spelled here נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙, the resh-family form) are all named before the battle-vision itself begins, and the fourth-year date sits header-internal rather than verse-initial. The battle-summons opens directly on the next verse with no intervening narration, עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.3, byte), matching “Prepare the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle!” (web:Jer.46.3), continuing אִסְר֣וּ הַסּוּסִ֗ים וַֽעֲלוּ֙ הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּכ֥וֹבָעִ֑ים מִרְקוּ֙ הָֽרְמָחִ֔ים לִבְשׁ֖וּ הַסִּרְיֹנֹֽת (oshb:Jer.46.4, byte), matching “Harness the horses, and get up, you horsemen, and stand up with your helmets. Polish the spears, put on the coats of mail.” (web:Jer.46.4) — imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants, not yet a named vocative. Shock at the rout follows, מַדּ֣וּעַ רָאִ֗יתִי הֵ֣מָּה חַתִּים֮ נְסֹגִ֣ים אָחוֹר֒ וְגִבּוֹרֵיהֶ֣ם יֻכַּ֔תּוּ וּמָנ֥וֹס נָ֖סוּ וְלֹ֣א הִפְנ֑וּ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִ֖יב נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.5, byte), matching “Why have I seen it? They are dismayed and are turned backward. Their mighty ones are beaten down, have fled in haste, and don’t look back. Terror is on every side," says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.46.5); the verse closes on neum-YHWH, but no fresh tier-1 onset follows it at the next verse, so the formula corroborates rather than closes a unit here, and the flight continues without a break, אַל יָנ֣וּס הַקַּ֔ל וְאַל יִמָּלֵ֖ט הַגִּבּ֑וֹר צָפ֨וֹנָה֙ עַל יַ֣ד נְהַר פְּרָ֔ת כָּשְׁל֖וּ וְנָפָֽלוּ (oshb:Jer.46.6, byte), matching “Don’t let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. In the north by the river Euphrates they have stumbled and fallen.” (web:Jer.46.6). A rhetorical question turns the description toward an extended Nile-simile, מִי זֶ֖ה כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֑ה כַּנְּהָר֕וֹת יִֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ מֵימָֽיו (oshb:Jer.46.7, byte), matching “Who is this who rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?” (web:Jer.46.7), and Egypt's own boast is quoted inside the same figure, מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֔ה וְכַנְּהָר֖וֹת יִתְגֹּ֣עֲשׁוּ מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַֽעֲלֶה֙ אֲכַסֶּה אֶ֔רֶץ אֹבִ֥ידָה עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.46.8, byte), matching “Egypt rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, ‘I will rise up. I will cover the earth. I will destroy cities and its inhabitants.’” (web:Jer.46.8). A summons to the allied troops follows, עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב וְיֵצְא֖וּ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים כּ֤וּשׁ וּפוּט֙ תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָגֵ֔ן וְלוּדִ֕ים תֹּפְשֵׂ֖י דֹּ֥רְכֵי קָֽשֶׁת (oshb:Jer.46.9, byte), matching “Go up, you horses! Rage, you chariots! Let the mighty men go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield; and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.” (web:Jer.46.9), and the scene is given its theological frame, וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת י֤וֹם נְקָמָה֙ לְהִנָּקֵ֣ם מִצָּרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֨רֶב֙ וְשָׂ֣בְעָ֔ה וְרָוְתָ֖ה מִדָּמָ֑ם כִּ֣י זֶ֠בַח לַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן אֶל נְהַר פְּרָֽת (oshb:Jer.46.10, byte), matching “For that day is of the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge himself of his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satiated, and will drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.” (web:Jer.46.10) — the construction לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is quoted here at the byte tier as its own prefixed token object, standing at two verses book-wide and recurring a second time later in this same verse (sweep: 2 verses). The first of the vision's three direct addresses to name its addressee falls next, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם לַשָּׁוְא֙ הרביתי הִרְבֵּ֣ית רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.46.11, byte), matching “Go up into Gilead, and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. You use many medicines in vain. There is no healing for you.” (web:Jer.46.11) — a named vocative, בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, to Egypt personified as a virgin daughter, distinct from the unnamed addressees of the plural imperatives at oshb:Jer.46.3 and oshb:Jer.46.9 (sweep: 3 verses: Jer.46.3, Jer.46.9, Jer.46.11), continuing the same battle-vision rather than opening a new one, and the verse itself carries a ketiv/qere pair, הרביתי written against הִרְבֵּ֣ית read (single-witness). The unit closes on a report of shared disgrace, שָׁמְע֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ קְלוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְצִוְחָתֵ֖ךְ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי גִבּ֤וֹר בְּגִבּוֹר֙ כָּשָׁ֔לוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו נָפְל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.46.12, byte), matching “The nations have heard of your shame, and the earth is full of your cry; for the mighty man has stumbled against the mighty, they both fall together.” (web:Jer.46.12), echoing back to verse 6's own flight-language with its own closing image of mutual collapse. oshb:Jer.46.12 itself carries a closing petuchah in the marked-verse layer (WLC-sourced, single witness only, weak in the Prophets by owner ruling). A differently-shaped header opens the next verse, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13), and this row stops short of that fresh onset.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The parashah inventory marks oshb:Jer.46.12 with a petuchah (WLC single witness; the Prophets addendum holds this tier-3 and never a driver). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own fresh word-event heading, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13) — the shape here is built on the verb דִּבֶּ֣ר ("spoke") rather than the verb hayah ("came/was") that underlies all three of the book's canonical word-event shapes, so it is disclosed as its own header device rather than folded into any of them. The heading opens directly onto a fresh summons to proclaim, הַגִּ֤ידוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וְהַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ בְמִגְדּ֔וֹל וְהַשְׁמִ֥יעוּ בְנֹ֖ף וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס אִמְר֗וּ הִתְיַצֵּב֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי אָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב סְבִיבֶֽיךָ (oshb:Jer.46.14, byte), matching “Declare in Egypt, publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes; say, ‘Stand up, and prepare, for the sword has devoured around you.’” (web:Jer.46.14) — imperatives addressed to the frontier garrison towns rather than to Egypt as a single named addressee. A rhetorical question follows without any new frame, מַדּ֖וּעַ נִסְחַ֣ף אַבִּירֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א עָמַ֔ד כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֲדָפֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.46.15, byte), matching “Why are your strong ones swept away? They didn’t stand, because Yahweh pushed them.” (web:Jer.46.15), and the mercenaries' own flight is reported in their own quoted words, הִרְבָּ֖ה כּוֹשֵׁ֑ל גַּם נָפַ֞ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ ק֣וּמָה וְנָשֻׁ֣בָה אֶל עַמֵּ֗נוּ וְאֶל אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.16, byte), matching “He made many to stumble. Yes, they fell on one another. They said, ‘Arise! Let’s go again to our own people, and to the land of our birth, from the oppressing sword.’” (web:Jer.46.16) — this verse itself carries a paseq (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The crowd's mockery of Pharaoh is quoted next, קָרְא֖וּ שָׁ֑ם פַּרְעֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ שָׁא֔וֹן הֶעֱבִ֖יר הַמּוֹעֵֽד (oshb:Jer.46.17, byte), matching “They cried there, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.’” (web:Jer.46.17), and the unit closes on a divine oath, חַי אָ֨נִי֙ נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא (oshb:Jer.46.18, byte), matching “As I live,” says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies, “surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, so he will come. (web:Jer.46.18) — the melekh-signature נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ, attributing the oath to the King whose name is Yahweh of Armies, names the oath's own speaker mid-verse rather than trailing it as a closing tag; it is one of only three sites of this exact construction in the book (sweep: 3 verses). The next verse opens on a fresh direct address, כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.46.19, byte), matching “You daughter who dwells in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity; for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.” (web:Jer.46.19), and this row stops at the oath that precedes it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating verse 13 as opening its own row alone, separate from the summons it introduces, was considered and rejected: oshb:Jer.46.13 carries its own topic clause, לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם, Nebuchadnezzar's coming to strike the land of Egypt, so the heading is not the content-free citation the rejected reading first supposed; even so, that content only names the topic the following summons carries out, matching how seven of the book's eleven ha-davar-asher-hayah header verses likewise carry topic content yet still open directly onto their first movement rather than standing as an isolated citation, the other four — oshb:Jer.7.1, oshb:Jer.11.1, oshb:Jer.18.1 and oshb:Jer.30.1 — being the content-free members of the class (sweep: 11 verses, 4 content-free / 7 content-bearing).
